speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; can you describe exactly how your spinning sensation started and if you experienced any nausea, hearing changes, or loss of balance?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The brief duration of three minutes and the sudden onset while lying down are classic for BPPV. Given your age and the absence of hearing loss or neurological deficits, do you notice any specific head movements, like rolling over in bed, that trigger the spinning sensation?
